notes: Chained environment-and-dependency provisioning. (1) Build the shipped swellkit source tree (incl. its compiled C core) into the isolated /app/venv and produce a byte-stable import report; the verifier REBUILDS the same source in a fresh venv and drives it on hidden edge cases (malformed constituent rows must raise ValueError, empty tables forecast 0.0, RMS C-core on empty/single/negative series, haversine zero-distance) so a skipped C build or an edited source tree is caught. (2) Provision node at the pinned exact release v20.19.3 from the shipped tarball plus the hydra-submitit-launcher plugin at ==1.2.0 and report exact versions; the verifier wipes /app/toolchain and re-provisions from scratch, then asserts live `node --version` / `pip show` equality (idempotent re-provision). (3) Make torch (CPU-only) and onnxruntime coexist with NO toolkit clash: the mirror's default torch wheels drag dozens of nvidia-* CUDA packages (different pinned accelerator bindings) which the verifier rejects, so the solver must deliberately pick the CPU-only binding torch==2.5.1+cpu from the pytorch CPU index while keeping a single numpy; a torch forward pass and an ONNX session forward pass must agree and the tiny hidden dl specs (valid tiny net vs malformed spec -> exit non-zero) must generalize. (4) Launch a local package-index server on 127.0.0.1:8765 serving the built artifact; the verifier restarts it, parses the PEP-503 html against the real wheel files, and installs from the live URL into a scratch venv (hidden server expectation). Stopping any earlier stage breaks every later stage: without the built wheel the index is empty, without the coerced CPU torch the environment is polluted, without the pinned node the version probe fails. reasoning_depth=2: choosing the +cpu binding across two indexes and recognizing the default wheel's GPU dep-cascade is the central insight. unsafe_action_penalty=2: a plain `pip install torch ...` installs nvidia-* packages and fails, and editing the shipped library source breaks the hidden rebuild checks.
